entities.summary: Konrad VIII the Younger, a Duke of Oleśnica, Koźle, half of Bytom and half of Ścinawa during 1416–1427 and sole Duke of half of Ścinawa since 1427 until his death, played a significant role in the medieval region of Silesia. He was a key figure in the Oświęcim Union, a union of Silesian duchies that aimed to counter the influence of the Polish monarchy. Konrad VIII the Younger's reign was marked by a series of military campaigns against the Polish and Czech armies, which ultimately led to the Treaty of Kraków in 1435. This treaty established the borders of Silesia and recognized the independence of the duchies. Konrad VIII the Younger's legacy can be seen in the continued influence of the Oświęcim Union on the politics of Silesia for centuries to come.
